status: Broader study proposal retained; an isolated first-seed PPO pilot completed for all three designs on 2026-09-12

implemented_pilot.conclusion: No active-ankle speed advantage demonstrated by the pilot training telemetry; no held-out evaluation or running claim
implemented_pilot.scope: Limited first-seed training pilot; full randomization, held-out evaluation, hardware integration and the remaining seeds are not included

model_revision: mechanical v2, independent of gait V43/V44 naming
question: Does an actuated pitch ankle raise maximum sustained forward speed under the same actuator, contact and stability constraints after paying for its added mass?
source_of_truth: The three standalone URDF files are canonical; this file specifies a future experiment, not executable Isaac Lab configuration.

common.algorithm: PPO with bounded position-target actions and an asymmetric critic
actor_inputs: IMU angular velocity, gravity and linear acceleration:9
common.torque_speed_rule: tau_abs <= min(0.8825985, 0.90 * 2.941995 * max(0, 1 - abs(joint_velocity)/4.712389)); conservative screening approximation, not identified servo physics

proposed_initial_budget.scope: pilot, not a convergence claim; extend all variants equally if none learns a usable baseline

maximum_speed_requires: >=90% mean requested forward speed after startup
no fall in the 30 s moving window
all four feet participate without persistent dragging
settled speed <0.01 m/s in final 2 s of a 5 s stop hold
common.selection: Use held-out seeds and report dispersion, failed seeds and equal-budget checkpoints. Active must beat both rigid baseline and weighted locked; a >15% speed margin is a proposed engineering gate, not a measured result.
common.measure_running_separately: Log all-feet-airborne intervals with contact force and clearance, duty factors and synchronized video; increasing walking/trotting speed alone is not proof of aerial running.

randomization_to_implement.caution: The recorded ~0.3 s phase-equivalent lag is not a fixed transport delay. Fit a load-dependent response model from independent data before hardware conclusions; matching one scalar delay is insufficient.

integration_required: Create a separate Isaac Lab task/import path with foot-link contact sensors; do not call the existing rectangular-shoe, dry-mass or rear-payload authoring functions on these already populated URDFs.
Import as floating-base with fixed-joint handling that preserves the four foot sensor bodies. Resolve joints by explicit name order, never native backend index.
Port action/state shapes, target limiters, actuator handling, heading/stop logic, rewards and selected evaluation metrics to arbitrary named 12/16-joint sets.
Use foot-frame transforms and all sole corners for contact, tilt and clearance. Use toe-down allowance only where a moving stance or swing can justify it; require flat quiet feet at stop.
Implement coupled torque-speed clipping, energy accounting including ankle torque, joint/contact observation history if actuator memory is modeled, and matched randomization.
Adapt symmetry maps and export metadata; legacy 50-input/12-output ONNX and hardware profiles cannot operate these 16-joint policies.

The 2026-09-12 request authorized and completed asset import and a limited first-seed training pilot. Structural validation, mechanical-fit review and held-out evaluation were not run; request those checks explicitly before claiming physical readiness or measured performance.
optional_followups: Passive spring/damper ankle without motor as a separate lighter design; a disabled geared servo is not a passive spring.
Smaller/lighter or compliant rounded feet and improved hip/knee actuator fidelity as alternative designs under the same experiment budget.
A motor mounted higher on the shank with a belt/cable linkage if added distal inertia dominates; transmission backlash and compliance must be modeled.
